summary: Feed s169_triple to NDR is degraded: 41.2% of TCP sessions are one-way, 4.2% TCP packets show drops, and 90.2% of bytes are encrypted just over the 90% tolerance. NDR requires both directions and full payload - one-way and drops break flow reassembly and detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/TAP is only delivering one direction for many flows - likely SPAN/mirror configured on a single direction or asymmetric routing where A->B and B->A take different paths and only one path is tapped without aggregation at the broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true). With 47 of 114 sessions one-way, TCP reassembly, request/response correlation, and anomaly detection fail - misses lateral movement, C2, and data exfiltration.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow at the packet broker so the NDR sees complete bidirectional sessions required for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: SPAN/mirror buffer oversubscription or congested packet broker link dropping packets before the tool - 56 of 1334 TCP packets show gaps/retransmissions (4.2% vs 1% threshold) while tool itself is not overloaded, so loss is in the visibility fabric.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload and complete streams. Missing segments cause TCP reassembly failures, broken file extraction, and missed IDS signatures - high false-negative risk.

recommended_fix.why: TAPs do not drop under load like SPAN buffers do; replacing SPAN with TAP eliminates fabric-induced drops and ensures complete packets to the NDR. If aggregate rate >10Gbps, add load_balance to NDR cluster.

findings.root_cause: 90.2% of bytes are TLS/encrypted, just above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is largely opaque without decryption - expected for modern networks but limits deep packet inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for detection; with almost all traffic encrypted it is blind to payload, can only do metadata/JA3/flow analysis and will miss payload-based threats.

params.evaluate: broker-based TLS decryption or feed decrypted copy via key escrow

recommended_fix.why: Decrypting at the packet broker (with proper privacy controls) restores payload visibility for the NDR without breaking end-to-end encryption elsewhere.
